note: Only sources from the challenge's Resources tab: the Mars Pathfinder mission page and the NSSDCA catalogue.

facts.text: Mars Pathfinder landed in Ares Vallis, Mars, on 4 July 1997, carrying the Sojourner rover.
Cushioned by airbags 5.8 metres across, Pathfinder bounced like a giant beach ball about 15 times, as high as 15 metres (50 feet), before coming to rest.
Pathfinder opened its three triangular solar-panel petals 87 minutes after landing.
Sojourner was 630 mm long, 480 mm wide and 280 mm high, with a mass of 10.5 kg. Standing at its full height it was 30 cm tall.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Rover (challenge catalogue); height from the NASA Science Mars Pathfinder page

facts.text: Mars Pathfinder delivered the first-ever robotic rover, Sojourner, to the Martian surface. Late on sol 2 it rolled down the lander's rear ramp.
The time delay between Earth and Mars was about 10 minutes, so the rover needed some control of its own.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Project Information (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: The rover was controlled by an operator on Earth using images from the rover and the lander; because of the delay it also had its own hazard avoidance system.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Rover (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: The team's rock names included Barnacle Bill, Yogi and Scooby Doo.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Preliminary Results (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: Sojourner's Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer (APXS) measured what rocks and soils are made of. The mission returned more than 15 chemical analyses of rocks and soil.
Barnacle Bill and Yogi (corrected for dust) plot in or near the field of andesites, a type of lava common at continental margins on Earth.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: APXS Composition Results (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: Yogi first appeared to be basalt, but it is covered with dust; with the dust subtracted, its composition is similar to Barnacle Bill's.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Preliminary Results (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: The APXS analysis of Scooby-Doo shows only minor differences from the local soils.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Preliminary Results (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: Rounded pebbles and cobbles at the landing site suggested conglomerates that formed in running water, during a warmer past when liquid water was stable.

The rover's primary objectives were scheduled for the first seven sols. It rolled onto Mars at about 05:40 UT on 6 July 1997 and worked until communications were lost on 27 September 1997: 83 days (our count from those two dates).
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Rover (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: The primary objectives were all planned within about 10 metres of the lander.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Rover (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: Pathfinder's final data transmission was on 27 September 1997. Communications were lost for unknown reasons.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Mars Pathfinder (challenge resource); reason from NASA NSSDCA

facts.text: All rover communications were done through the lander, over a UHF radio link.
facts.sourceName: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Pathfinder Rover (challenge catalogue)

facts.text: The twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity landed on Mars in 2004; the Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet on 19 April 2021.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: Spirit and Opportunity, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (challenge resources)

facts.text: Mars Pathfinder's landing site, and the place its mission ended, is Ares Vallis.
